function.description:
Search the web; results contain summaries and partial page content. Review evidence, fetch_url promising pages for details, then refine if needed. Batch independent searches with queries:[{query,freshness?,vertical?}]; they run concurrently. When queries is present, top-level query is ignored.

Auto vertical enrichment recognizes CVE IDs (CVE-2024-1234), arXiv IDs (2301.07041), DOIs (10.1038/s41586-023-06221-2), stock tickers (AAPL/$TSLA), pypi:requests, npm:express, github:facebook/react, and IPs (8.8.8.8). HF daily/trending papers uses query wording for day/week/month; related-work/citation queries use Semantic Scholar. Vertical records accompany Web results. freshness affects only Web results, best-effort per engine, never the HF time window.

**Explicit vertical**: set ``vertical='<domain>'`` to force one source.
- ``academic`` — Papers, citations and related work.
- ``code`` — Package and repository metadata.
- ``finance`` — Live quote and recent price history.
- ``security`` — Vulnerability details from NVD/NIST.
- ``network`` — IP geolocation and owning organisation.
- ``travel`` — Real bookable travel inventory — flights and hotels with live prices.
function.name: web_search

freshness.description: Best-effort time filter on the WEB results only (some engines ignore it; does not affect vertical sources). Only use when the user explicitly wants recent results.

queries.description: Array of search queries (for batch mode). All queries run concurrently. Much faster than multiple separate web_search calls. Each element MUST be an object like {"query": "..."} — never a single bare string or a concatenation of queries; for one search use the top-level 'query' field instead.

freshness.description: Time filter for this specific query

vertical.description: Force a vertical data source for this query. 'off' = web only. See the tool description for per-domain coverage.

query.description: Search query — be specific and targeted. Single-search mode; omit when using 'queries'.

vertical.description: Force a vertical data source. 'auto' (default) phrase-detects. 'off' = web only. See the tool description for what each domain covers and which need an identifier.

function.description: Read remote HTTP(S) HTML/PDF/text; follow relevant Page Links. Local paths/file://: read_files. Text supports artifact paging; binaries return server-staging paths. If HTTP lacks login, the selected browser streams bytes to staging, never browser Downloads. Use an authorized filesystem tool to copy/move and verify receipt. Concurrent batch urls:[{url}]: url ignored; extract: single mode. extract returns quote-backed findings and unresolved requests from bounded windows; gaps do not prove absence. Raw source stays artifact-readable; failure returns raw.
function.name: fetch_url

url.description: Single HTTP(S) URL; omit with urls.

urls.description: Concurrent batch of {url} objects; url ignored.

function.description: Read one or more files with line numbers and optional ranges. Read WIDE within the round budget: for 1-2 relevant files request 200+ lines or a whole small file instead of repeated 50-line fragments; for 3+ files use focused ranges or `search_files`. An explicit start/end range is authoritative and never widened. Whole-file text reads retain complete sources; model previews are budgeted separately. Batch independent ranges while keeping expected model content near 24k tokens; every requested read executes. Use top-level `path` for one file. Prefer this over shell cat/head/tail/sed. Relative paths use the project; absolute, `~`, and `file://` paths are supported. Images are shown natively; PDFs extract layout text; Office files extract Markdown text/tables; text uses encoding detection.
function.name: read_files

bind_sources.description: Opt in to exact UTF-8 project file sources for working facts. Returns id/version/path; add a quote when recording a fact. Unsupported sources are explicit. Hashes the whole file even for ranged reads; default false.

end_line.description: End line (inclusive, optional) — only with top-level 'path'.

path.description: Single-file path; ignored when `reads` is present. Relative, absolute, and `~` supported.

reads.description: Batch file/range specs: `{path, start_line?, end_line?}`. Every requested read executes.

path.description: Relative or absolute file path; supports `~`.

start_line.description: Start line (1-based, optional) — only with top-level 'path'.

function.description: Read fine detail by transforming the ORIGINAL image at source resolution before model downscaling. Read the whole image once, then inspect ONE crop/zoom region per call; many returned images are downscaled together. Use grid=true first for 0–1 coordinates, then crop. READ-ONLY; never changes the source.
function.name: inspect_image

crop.description: Keep [x0,y0,x1,y1]. Each 0–1 value is its axis fraction; >1 is pixels, and units may mix. Coordinates follow the visible frame after EXIF orientation then rotate. [.5,0,1,.5] is the top-right quadrant. Crop wins over zoom; omit for the whole frame. Prefer grid fractions.

grid.description: Overlay labelled 0–1 coordinates for a later crop; default false.

path.description: Local path using read_files rules (png/jpg/jpeg/gif/webp/bmp), or a chat upload's shown /api/images/<file> reference. Do not invent a path such as /dev/null.

rotate.description: Clockwise degrees after EXIF orientation; default 0.

zoom.description: Centre zoom >1; 2 keeps the middle quarter. Used only when crop is omitted.

function.description: Search project file content and return paths, line numbers, and matches. Prefer this over shell grep/rg: a persistent file index plus ripgrep over exact candidates avoids recursive walks on huge/network (FUSE) trees, includes hidden files, skips ignored paths unless `path` is inside one, and is case-insensitive by default. Prefer short literal keywords; regex uses Rust/ripgrep syntax (`A|B`, `\.` for a literal dot, per-line `^`/`$`), not GNU BRE. `path` is one relative path or project root. For independent roots/patterns use one `searches` batch; every operation runs and avoids sequential model rounds.
function.name: search_files

context_lines.description: Lines before/after each match. Default 0, max 10; use 3-5 to avoid a follow-up read.

count_only.description: Return the full matching-line count only; `max_results` is ignored in count_only mode.

from_line.description: Only report matches on lines ≥ N (per-file floor for paging).

max_results.description: Matching-line cap, default 50; use 5-20 for samples/existence checks.

path.description: One relative path; omit for project root.

pattern.description: Short literal substring preferred; Rust/ripgrep regex is supported.

searches.description: Batch operations; all entries execute. Faster than separate calls.

function.description:
Find files by name pattern (glob) in the project. Useful for discovering test files, configs, etc.

**Prefer this over ``run_command find``** — find_files is served from a persistent project file index (near-instant even on huge or network-mounted trees), supports ``max_results``, includes hidden files, and auto-filters ignored paths (node_modules, .venv, .gitignore matches, etc.) unless ``path`` points inside one.

For MULTIPLE searches, provide a 'searches' array — each entry has the same fields as the top-level parameters. Batch mode cuts round trips.
function.name: find_files

max_results.description: Maximum number of files to return. Default 100. Use a small value (5-20) when you only need a quick sample.

searches.description: Array of find operations. All entries execute with the same fields as the top-level parameters. Faster than separate find_files calls.

function.description:
Return a compact structural outline of the project: which source files define which functions/classes/methods, ranked by how often other files reference them. Use this FIRST when you need to orient in an unfamiliar area — it is much cheaper than repeated ls/grep rounds. The map contains ONLY definition lines (signature + 1-based line number), never bodies; hand its paths and line numbers to read_files to see the actual code. Read-only, makes no changes.

Filters: `path` scopes the map to one subdirectory (e.g. "lib/storage"); `focus` keeps only files whose path contains the given text. Returns all definitions in the selected scope; shared L0 handles long results without producer truncation.

Both filters are optional: call with `{}` to map the whole project.
function.name: repo_map

focus.description: Case-insensitive substring filter on file paths (e.g. "storage" or "_test.py"). Optional.

path.description: Project-relative subdirectory to map (default: whole project). Use this on huge repos to zoom in.

function.description: Create or replace one whole file, or append to its end. For new files/major rewrites; use edit_file for mid-file changes. Set append=true to append to the end (a missing file is created): send only the new bytes, no read or anchor needed. Read an existing file first and supply its complete replacement—omitted lines are deleted. Relative paths use the current project. An absolute path outside registered roots needs allow_outside_workspace=true after the user confirms it (the containing directory then registers as a new root); system paths (/etc, /usr, $HOME itself) are refused outright. Give exactly one source: content (an empty string creates an empty file) or content_ref to reuse all/a slice of a previous tool result.
function.name: write_file

allow_outside_workspace.description: Set true only after the user explicitly confirmed this exact out-of-workspace destination; its containing directory registers as a new root. Default false: refused with an error naming this flag.

append.description: Append content to the end of the file instead of replacing it. Default false.

content_ref.description: Reuse prior tool output without regenerating it.

description.description: Optional pre-write caption shown before execution. Omit it to use the file-path label.

path.description: Project-relative or allowed absolute file path.

function.description: Apply ordered anchored edits; read/write targets in an earlier round. Prefer replace, including additions: content is the complete desired replacement, including retained anchor text and all line breaks. After A: `{"operation":"replace","anchor":"A","content":"A\nB"}`; before A: `{"operation":"replace","anchor":"A","content":"B\nA"}`. For insert_after/insert_before, content is only new text; the anchor stays automatically. Append at end-of-file with write_file(append=true). Name the batch's file once in `path` and leave each edit's own `path` out; set an edit's `path` only to target a different file. Anchors match exactly once; replace_all permits multiple matches only for replace. Later edits see earlier changes. Atomic preflight defaults true: any validation failure writes nothing. With atomic=false, one failure neither rolls back nor stops the others. I/O failures may leave partial writes.
function.name: edit_file

allow_outside_workspace.description: Set true only after the user explicitly confirmed this exact out-of-workspace destination; its containing directory registers as a new root. Default false: refused.

atomic.description: Preflight all edits before writing. False permits partial application.

description.description: Optional pre-edit caption (max 120 chars). Omit it to use the file-path label.

anchor.description: Exact, normally unique existing text. For replace, this is the old text being removed.

content.description: Replace: complete new text, including anchor parts to keep and all newlines; empty to delete. Insert: added lines only, without copied anchor/context.

operation.description: Prefer replace for complete old-to-new edits, including additions. insert_after adds content below anchor; insert_before above it.

path.description: File for this edit, when it differs from the batch `path`. Never inherited from the previous edit; omit it rather than sending an empty string.

replace_all.description: Replace every match; ignored by inserts.

path.description: File this batch edits. Write it once here for a single-file batch instead of repeating it on every edit; an edit's own `path` overrides it.

function.description:
Run builds, tests, lint, installs, Git or pipelines; returns stdout/stderr. NO timeout: runs until it finishes, the user stops it, or you stop a backgrounded one with `kill`. Execution may move to the background on new messages; results arrive automatically. Avoid waiting for stdin.

Fresh subprocess; no persistent shell or environment changes. Prefer absolute paths and `working_dir` over `cd`.

Use `read_files`, `search_files`, `find_files`, `edit_file`, `write_file` for repository data. Filesystem grep uses a bounded FUSE-safe engine or returns a `search_files` translation; filtering command output is allowed. `browser_download_url_to_server` handles authenticated browser downloads. Text helpers: `sd`, `mlr`, `goawk`.

Never use a shell no-op as a placeholder (`true`, `:`, `exit 0`); repetition is a tool loop.
function.name: run_command

background.description: Start in background and return a command_id handle. Completion is delivered automatically — end the turn or do other work. `poll` reads its status or waits for it; `kill` stops it.

command.description: Shell command, for example `pytest` or `git status`.

credentials.description: Vault entry names for THIS child process only; use names from <credential_vault>. Values never enter the command/chat.

description.description: Short user-language caption: what runs and why.

working_dir.description: Optional directory. In multi-root workspaces use `rootname:subdir`. STICKY: an explicit `working_dir` becomes the default for later run_command calls in this conversation; a `cd` INSIDE a command never persists. Default: the explicit sticky directory, then the project root.

function.description: Render one page in a headless browser ON THE SERVER; return screenshot, console, uncaught JS errors, and failed requests. Use after frontend edits for layout/runtime. Give exactly one source: a project-relative .html path, served from project root so relative assets/ES modules work and external requests are blocked/reported; or an HTTP(S) url such as a dev server. Not for text (use fetch_url/browser_read_page) or the user's browser extension.
function.name: browser_preview_page

full_page.description: Capture the full scrollable page; default false.

wait_ms.description: Settle after DOM load in ms; default 1500.

function.description: Search other conversations when the user explicitly asks for past-conversation information. A bound project Coordinator may also inspect same-owner, same-project worker evidence needed to delegate, review or follow the current authorized request. Otherwise do not browse history proactively. Project mode scopes to siblings; scope=all requires an explicit user request beyond that project. The current conversation is never listed; the result names its ID for get_conversation. A keyword match in message text names the matching Turn ID and a snippet (also for the current conversation); read that page with get_conversation(conversation_id, turn_id).
function.name: list_conversations

function.description:
Retrieve a conversation by ID when the user explicitly requests past-conversation information. A bound project Coordinator may also inspect same-owner, same-project worker evidence needed to delegate, review or follow the current authorized request. Otherwise do not browse history proactively. Use an ID from list_conversations or the current assignment/result evidence.

The current conversation's own ID needs no user request: it returns this conversation's durable transcript, including Turns that may be outside your current working view (for example after compaction). Page to those older Turns with before=N.

To read a specific Turn (for example a list_conversations match), pass turn_id: the page around that Turn, with older/newer before=N hints in the header.

`raw` defaults to true: a structured, unsummarized DB record with row metadata/settings and every field of each delivered message, including full tool rounds. Set `raw=false` only for a readable transcript; it drops per-message metadata and condenses tool rounds.

Long histories return a parseable head+tail window of whole messages. Check `DELIVERED N of M`; use its positive `before=N` hint for older pages. `limit` widens the window but may clamp fields, which the header reports.
function.name: get_conversation

before.description: Exclusive 1-based end cursor (min 1) for an older page. Omit for latest; use the header's positive before=N hint. Never pass 0.

conversation_id.description: Conversation ID, usually from list_conversations; the current conversation's own ID reads its durable transcript.

include_tool_details.description: For raw=false only, include full tool arguments/results (default true); false shortens them. Raw mode always includes them.

limit.description: Recent-message count (min 1). Omit for a budget-fit whole-message window; too large may clamp fields, reported in the header.

raw.description: Default true: structured raw record with all fields of each delivered message. False returns readable prose that drops message metadata and condenses tool rounds.

turn_id.description: Read the page containing this main-transcript Turn, e.g. a Turn ID named by a list_conversations match. Exclusive with before.

function.description: Capture the current isolated writer workspace as a checkpoint. The runtime binds this call to this execution's automatic work ID.
function.name: integration_checkpoint

function.description: Save a checkpoint of this execution. Automatic task changes are merged into the current canonical workspace at successful completion, independently of commits and release gates. Explicit candidate submissions retain their review/checker policy.
function.name: integration_submit

summary.description: What changed and how it was verified.

function.description: Send bounded agent-authored context or a scoped request to an explicitly known same-project conversation. Commits durably, but starts no model call or worker. Idle recipients see it at their next authorized turn. Use get_project_messages to read actual input and consideration receipts. Agent text grants no human authority. Preserve the same idempotency_key/content after uncertainty. Use reply_to only for a message exchanged between the same two participants; no transcript access is implied. Subagents must ask their delegating parent to relay.
function.name: send_project_message

function.description: Read a bounded incoming or outgoing mailbox for this same-project conversation. Does not read private transcripts or start work. State input_confirmed is distinct from an explicit recipient consideration decision, and accepted is not proof of execution or delivery. Do not busy-poll. A conversation_id is required for outgoing; it identifies the recipient mailbox.
function.name: get_project_messages

function.description: Record your explicit accepted/rejected/deferred/conflict decision for an incoming message and explain why. Reads the immutable original message; this action never starts another worker, grants tools, or proves delivery. accepted is a stated commitment only and does not authorize new external side effects. Use expected_revision from get_project_messages; a conflict requires reading current authority, not overwriting another decision. No automatic ACK-of-ACK notification is generated.
function.name: consider_project_message

function.description: Stage one remote file ON THE TOFU SERVER for download/save/install/unzip/export/copy. Supply its exact HTTP(S) url. text/selector (+ optional tab_id) instead names an , data-download-url or /
function.name: browser_download_url_to_server

selector.description: Exact link/media CSS selector; wins over text.

tab_id.description: Open-page tab; omit for the working tab.

url.description: Exact HTTP(S) file URL; keep its signed query.

function.description: Watch a local video or hear an audio file: probe facts, timestamped key frames as images (video) and, when speech-to-text is available, a transcript. Pass start/end seconds to inspect one section densely. Read-only.
function.name: inspect_video

path.description: Project-relative or absolute path (e.g. a data/fetched/ file from fetch_url or browser_download_url_to_server), or an att_media_<id> chat video reference.

function.description: Check (and optionally bootstrap) the motion-video render environment: Node>=22, the HyperFrames CLI (auto-installed pinned version when missing), ffmpeg, ffprobe (optional), and a headless Chrome. Call this first when a motion_video_* tool reports env_missing, or before your first render on a fresh deployment. Before authoring your first scene, read the vendored guides lib/motion_video/guide/WORKFLOW.md and COMPOSITION_CONTRACT.md (absolute paths under the tofu install) and start each scene from lib/motion_video/guide/skeleton.html. For one-take films with objects/camera carried between beats, read CONTINUOUS_FILM.md and start from guide/continuous/ (one index.html + continuity.json, no clip concat).
function.name: motion_video_env_check

install.description: When true (default), auto-install the pinned HyperFrames CLI into the tofu data dir if it is missing. First install downloads npm packages and can take a minute.

function.description: Zero-LLM gate: validate a scenes.json storyboard against its SRT transcript — required fields, monotonic contiguity, FULL coverage of the SRT span, and scene-duration sum equal to the span within ±0.1s. MANDATORY before rendering any scene. Returns a list of human-readable errors (empty = pass).
function.name: motion_video_storyboard_check

scenes_path.description: Path to scenes.json — a list of {id, start, end, text, visual?} with float seconds.

srt_path.description: Path to the SRT transcript (project-relative or absolute).

function.description: Run the HyperFrames static gates (lint + headless-Chrome validate + layout inspect) on one scene or whole-film project dir. MANDATORY before rendering. If continuity.json is present, also sample each declared handoff in a real browser: persistent DOM identity, visibility, geometry and reverse-seek pixel repeatability. Returns boundary contact-sheet paths for visual review. On failure returns categorized errors with upstream fix hints — repair the composition in place and re-check (max 2 repair rounds).
function.name: motion_video_check

function.description: Render one scene OR one continuous whole-film composition to MP4 via HyperFrames. Opted-in continuity.json handoffs must pass browser checks; render refuses failed/unavailable evidence. No concat is needed for a continuous film. Cost is ~3.5x realtime on this host (a 10s scene ≈ 35s). Use quality 'draft' while iterating, 'standard' for delivery, 'high' for final takes. After rendering, verify with motion_video_probe (resolution/fps/duration/silence).
function.name: motion_video_render

output.description: Output MP4 path (project-relative or absolute, e.g. .tofu/motion_video/<slug>/scenes/scene-001/scene-001.mp4).

timeout.description: Wall-clock seconds before the render is killed (default 1800; 0 = no limit).

function.description: Probe a media file (ffprobe, ffmpeg fallback): codec, resolution, fps, duration, audio-track presence. Use after every render and after concat to verify specs.
function.name: motion_video_probe

function.description: Assemble final.mp4 from ordered scene MP4s. Uniform specs concat losslessly (-c copy); mismatched scenes are re-encode-normalized to the first scene's spec. Optional transitions execute real FFmpeg xfade edits. For every overlap, the outgoing scene MUST already include an equal visual tail handle; then the final program duration stays aligned with narration/SRT. Output is atomic and post-verified.
function.name: motion_video_concat

transitions.description: Optional ordered N-1 boundary plan. Zero duration is a hard cut; non-zero boundaries consume an equal outgoing visual handle from the previous clip.

function.description: P2 音画合成 step 1: synthesize per-scene TTS narration WAVs from a storyboard scenes.json. Returns an alignment manifest — in the default 'loose' mode each scene's target_duration = max(srt, audio + tail_pad); when target_duration exceeds the SRT duration you MUST update that scene's data-duration before rendering. Degrades gracefully (ok=false, degraded=true) when no TTS slot is configured — deliver the silent video.
function.name: motion_video_narrate

alignment.description: 'loose' (default): scene duration follows the audio. 'strict': SRT span is fixed; over-long narration is reported as overflow for you to shorten the text.

function.description: Final audio step. With audio_plan_path, stage and hash licensed local BGM/SFX, resolve cues against scenes/beat time, duck BGM under narration, mix to -14 LUFS, and emit audio_plan.json + audio_attribution.txt. Without a plan, mux the single narration track using the legacy loudnorm path. Runtime audio downloads are forbidden. Post-verified: audio present and program duration preserved.
function.name: motion_video_mux

audio.description: Optional narration track. Required when no audio plan is provided; optional for BGM/SFX-only delivery.

audio_plan_path.description: Optional motion-audio-v1 JSON, relative to the project or absolute. Its asset paths resolve beside the plan.

loudnorm.description: Apply EBU R128 loudness normalization (default true).

scenes_path.description: scenes.json carrying motion-timeline-v1 fields; required for scene-relative SFX cues.

function.description: Produce a short science-explainer VIDEO from a single topic or news headline — fully automatic, no storyboard or SRT needed. The pipeline researches the topic on the web (every claim is grounded in a real source URL and credited on an end card), writes a spoken script, times it to real TTS narration, and renders a narrated vertical MG video. Returns immediately with a task_id; the video generates in the background (a few minutes) and the user watches progress in the video panel. Use this when the user asks for a video ABOUT something and has not supplied their own script/SRT/storyboard. Does NOT require an attached project. This is an agent-based tool with an authored workflow: internal models work within fixed stages, with output validation, domain quality checks and durable checkpoints. Call it directly from normal Chat; no Goal mode or free-form agent delegation is needed. A returned task_id confirms acceptance, not delivery. Continue other requested work and let the task panel report progress; do not repeatedly poll or claim a finished artifact from the acceptance receipt.
function.name: produce_video

creative_mode.description: Planning strategy. 'director' (DEFAULT) drafts two contrasting evidence/visual plans, gates both, and uses an independent critic to select the stronger one. 'standard' makes one planning call and is the lower-cost A/B control.

max_scenes.description: Upper bound on scene count / cost (3..12, default 8). Exceeding it degrades gracefully.

model.description: Optional model id that locks both the script writer and every scene author, for example 'kimi-k3'.

narration.description: TTS voice-over (default true; degrades to a silent video when no TTS slot is configured).

topic.description: The subject or news headline to explain, e.g. '为什么天空是蓝色的' or 'the James Webb telescope's latest exoplanet finding'.

visual_quality.description: 'authored' (DEFAULT) gives every scene its own small agent that writes a bespoke composition with real typographic hierarchy, staggered entrances and supporting graphics. 'template' is the fast zero-LLM fallback card (one centred line on a gradient) — pass it only when the user explicitly wants speed over looks. A scene whose authoring fails may fall back to a template and be marked degraded. Final task status and quality determine whether the film was delivered.

function.description: Produce a long-form RESEARCH REPORT from a single topic — fully automatic. The pipeline researches the topic on the web (every claim grounded in a real source URL), drafts an outline, writes each section, and assembles a cited markdown report published as an artifact. Returns immediately with a task_id; the report generates in the background. Use this when the user wants a written deep-dive / report / briefing on a subject rather than a quick chat answer. Does NOT require an attached project. This is an agent-based tool with an authored workflow: internal models work within fixed stages, with output validation, domain quality checks and durable checkpoints. Call it directly from normal Chat; no Goal mode or free-form agent delegation is needed. A returned task_id confirms acceptance, not delivery. Continue other requested work and let the task panel report progress; do not repeatedly poll or claim a finished artifact from the acceptance receipt.
function.name: produce_report

depth.description: brief ≈3 sections, standard ≈5, deep ≈8. Deeper costs more and takes longer.

topic.description: The subject to research and report on.

function.description: Develop candidate RESEARCH IDEAS in a field — the automated research pipeline. Given a research direction it harvests the recent literature into a local paper corpus (parsed once, then reused), surveys it to map what has already been done, and proposes scored ideas screened against that inspected corpus. Novelty and value judgments are provisional and limited to the retrieved evidence. The output is a survey and candidate ideas; research conclusions require reproducible baseline and candidate experiments, independent validation and inspection of originals. Continue the user goal through those stages before claiming empirical gains or publication readiness. Returns immediately with a task_id; the survey runs in the background (several minutes). Use this when the user asks what is worth working on, wants research directions / open problems / a gap analysis in a field — NOT for a written summary of a topic (that is produce_report). Does NOT require an attached project. This is an agent-based tool with an authored workflow: internal models work within fixed stages, with output validation, domain quality checks and durable checkpoints. Call it directly from normal Chat; no Goal mode or free-form agent delegation is needed. A returned task_id confirms acceptance, not delivery. Continue other requested work and let the task panel report progress; do not repeatedly poll or claim a finished artifact from the acceptance receipt.
function.name: produce_research

direction.description: The research direction to mine for open problems, e.g. 'long-context KV cache compression' or '扩散模型的推理加速'.

n_ideas.description: How many ideas to generate and score (3..12, default 6). Ideas that fail the novelty screen against the corpus are reported as rejected, with the reason.

seed_arxiv_ids.description: Optional arXiv ids to seed the corpus with, e.g. ['2312.00752']. Use when the user names specific papers to start from.

function.description: Produce a polished, DESIGNER-QUALITY slide deck (PPTX) from a single topic — fully automatic. The pipeline classifies the scenario (tech / business / academic / education / brand / report / analysis), binds ONE curated theme (palette + licensed CJK/Latin typefaces + the scenario's design bible), authors every page in the PPTD layout language, renders per-page previews, runs a multimodal visual-QA pass, and exports a NATIVE, fully editable .pptx (real text boxes, shapes, tables — not page images) with fade transitions. Returns immediately with a task_id; the deck generates in the background and the user watches progress. Use this whenever the user asks for a PPT / slide deck / presentation / 幻灯片 / 课件 / 路演. Does NOT require an attached project. This is an agent-based tool with an authored workflow: internal models work within fixed stages, with output validation, domain quality checks and durable checkpoints. Call it directly from normal Chat; no Goal mode or free-form agent delegation is needed. A returned task_id confirms acceptance, not delivery. Continue other requested work and let the task panel report progress; do not repeatedly poll or claim a finished artifact from the acceptance receipt.
function.name: produce_slides

creative_mode.description: Planning strategy. 'director' (DEFAULT) drafts two contrasting deck plans, gates both, and uses an independent critic to select the stronger one. 'standard' is the single-plan A/B control.

material.description: Optional caller-supplied source material (up to 20000 chars) the deck MUST be grounded in — a content brief, resume, project report or notes. Use this whenever the deck must reflect the user's OWN work, numbers and attributions rather than public web research: its facts and figures are treated as authoritative and are never replaced by web results or invented values. Keep 'topic' as the short deck title.

max_pages.description: Upper bound on page count / cost (3..20, default 12).

model.description: Optional model id that locks the outline, page authors and repair rounds, for example 'kimi-k3'.

function.description: Edit ONE or SEVERAL pages of a deck created by produce_slides, in plain language — e.g. '第 3 页标题改成…', 'make page 2 dark', '给第 5 页加一个柱状图'. Each page is re-authored from its CURRENT layout (everything else stays), re-validated, re-rendered and the PPTX is re-exported once at the end. Use this for content rewrites / layout restructuring; for simple field-level changes (改文字/字号/颜色/图片) prefer patch_slides (deterministic, no LLM, seconds). Pass `page` for one page or `pages` for a batch (≤8) sharing one instruction.

instruction.description: What to change on that page, in the user's words.

function.description: Edit ONE scene of a video created by produce_video, in plain language — e.g. '把第 2 个镜头的标题改成…', 'make scene 3 slower and darker', '给第 4 镜换成柱状图表达'. Two modes: 'rewrite' (default) has the scene author rewrite that scene's composition from its CURRENT frame (everything else stays; the better of old/new wins), then only that scene is re-rendered and the final video re-assembled in place. 'set_narration' replaces the scene's spoken narration text deterministically (new TTS must FIT the scene's existing duration — shorten the text when it overflows); the frame is untouched and only the audio/subtitles rebuild. Returns immediately with an edit task_id. Use this for follow-up edits instead of regenerating the whole film. Scene numbers are 1-based (scene-001 … scene-NNN also accepted).
function.name: edit_video

asset_kind.description: swap_asset: fetch stock media (default), AI-generate a still, or 't2v' — a text-to-video CLIP (video targets only, needs TOFU_T2V_* configured).

instruction.description: rewrite: what to change in that scene, in the user's words. set_narration: the NEW narration text for the scene. set_subtitle_style: a short note (may be a placeholder like '字幕样式'). swap_asset: the QUERY describing the replacement asset.

model.description: Optional model id locking the scene author for this edit (rewrite only).

op.description: Edit mode (default 'rewrite'). set_subtitle_style is JOB-LEVEL (scene may be omitted) and needs `style`.

target.description: swap_asset: the scene's current media path to replace (required only when the scene references several media files).

function.description: DETERMINISTIC field-level edits to ONE page of a deck created by produce_slides — zero LLM, applies in seconds, fully predictable. PREFER this over edit_slides whenever the user's request maps to a field mutation: 改标题/正文文字 (set_text), 调字号/颜色/加粗 (set_style), 挪位置/改大小 (set_bounds), 换图片 (swap_image), 删元素 (delete), 复制元素 (duplicate). Targets are elementId / componentId shown in the page source; use edit_slides instead when the change needs rewriting copy, restructuring the layout, or editing component internals beyond metric/quote/code scalar fields. function.description: Deck-LEVEL deterministic restyle of a deck created by produce_slides — zero LLM, re-renders in seconds. PREFER this whenever the user asks to restyle the WHOLE deck: 换主题 (theme_id), 换配色 (colors), 换字体 (fonts). The deck's elements reference theme tokens precisely so the entire visual language changes without rewriting one page. Do NOT re-run produce_slides for a restyle.

function.description: Undo a conversational deck edit: restore the deck to the snapshot taken before a patch_slides / restyle_slides / edit_slides step (versions are listed in every edit result, newest first). The restored deck is re-validated, every page re-rendered and the PPTX re-exported. Reverting keeps the snapshot — the user can bounce between versions.

function.name: load_skill

function.description: Read a complete UTF-8 resource (or suffix at cursor) using an opaque skill:// path listed by load_skill. Do not convert workspace file paths into skill:// URIs. Binary, oversized, symlinked, or escaping paths are rejected.

resource.description: Package-relative path or skill://<id>/<path> from load_skill. Never a workspace file path.

function.description: Request installation of one exact verified catalog match from search_skills. Manual mode requires user confirmation; Auto mode authorizes verified installation, up to three attempts per task. Successful installation also loads its whole guide. It never runs bundled scripts. Do not call for unavailable entries.

function.description:
Register a calendar job that fires on a clock. Waiters use timer_create. Use local-time five-field cron `minute hour day month weekday` for recurrence, or `once:YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM` for one run and auto-disable. Examples: `*/5 * * * *`, `0 9 * * 1-5`. Cron repeats until disabled; max_executions=1 also makes it one-shot. For approximate times avoid :00/:30 contention and choose an off-minute such as :07; honor an exact user-specified time.
Types: command=shell and python=code (either may be disabled by deployment), prompt=one LLM call without tools, agent=clock-triggered independent polls followed by a visible full-tool turn in the target conversation. Use agent for monitoring, recurring analysis, or event triggers.
function.name: schedule_create

command.description: Shell/Python/prompt payload; for agent, the standing trigger and action instruction. For a pure-code agent with condition_command, pass an empty string.

condition_command.description: Agent-only decisive shell predicate: exit 0 acts, or condition_regex matches stdout. With empty command it is zero-LLM code polling; with a standing instruction it is hybrid and auto-promotes to code after agreement. Prefer for deterministic triggers.

condition_regex.description: Agent-only readiness regex over predicate stdout; omit to use exit code 0.

max_runtime.description: Max seconds before killing (default 300, not used for 'agent')

target_conv_id.description: Required for agent: target conversation ID; use current for this conversation.

task_type.description: command (default), python, prompt, or proactive agent.

tools_config.description: Agent tool settings. Keys: searchMode, fetchEnabled, projectPath, codeExecEnabled, browserEnabled, memoryEnabled, imageGenEnabled. Missing keys inherit target-conversation settings; the model always follows the target conversation.

function.description: List all scheduled tasks with their status, next run time, and execution history.
function.name: schedule_list

function.description:
Manage a scheduled task: run immediately, enable/disable, delete, or update.
Actions: 'run' (trigger now), 'enable', 'disable', 'delete', 'update', 'log' (view execution log)
function.name: schedule_manage

updates.description: Fields to update (for 'update' action): name, schedule, command, task_type, description, max_runtime

function.description: Manage Timer Watchers — cancel, check status, list active timers, or view the poll log.
function.name: timer_manage

action.description:
'cancel' — cancel an active timer
'status' — get details of a specific timer
'list' — list all timers
'log' — view poll log for a timer

function.description:
Start a readiness watcher that injects one continuation. For deferred follow-ups. Cron/once jobs use schedule_create. Durable single-shot: return immediately; do not wait or poll manually. Survives tasks and server restarts. timer_manage exposes evidence; ready starts a fresh authoritative turn with continuation_message and auto-disables when ready.
Only self-resolving external conditions (CI/job/file/download), never a human-only action such as restarting/redeploying this Tofu server; stop and ask the user, verify after they act. Polls are independent with no cross-poll history and can use the same search, shell, and file tools as this task.
function.name: timer_create

check_command.description: Optional evidence command; output informs but does not decide readiness.

check_instruction.description: Optional tool-capable poll LLM instruction: exact target/source, ready/error criteria. Omit only with condition_command.

condition_command.description: Decisive shell predicate: exit 0 is ready, 1 waits, other exits error; condition_regex matches successful stdout instead. Cheapest zero-LLM for deterministic conditions. With check_instruction: hybrid retains model verification.

condition_regex.description: Readiness regex over successful condition_command stdout; omit to use exit code 0.

continuation_message.description: Required user message injected when ready for a full tool-capable turn. Specify the next action.

function.description: Inspect an earlier interrupted write_file occurrence in this conversation. Use the exact operation_id and producing turn_id or invocation_id from its recovery instruction. The result is file_published (historical publication, not current content), file_not_published (proved at inspection), or unknown. This read never repeats a write, authorizes retry, resumes an invocation, or accepts a task.
function.name: inspect_tool_effect

invocation_id.description: Registered producing child invocation; mutually exclusive with turn_id.

turn_id.description: Producing Turn ID; defaults to this task’s Turn.

function.description: Read one or more bounded ranges from prior large tool results. Omitted row artifactRef inherits its page's reference.
function.name: read_tool_artifact

limit.description: UTF-8 bytes to return (1–65536); codepoints stay whole.
UTF-8 bytes to return (1–65536); codepoints stay whole.

selector.description: Optional RFC6901 JSON pointer into JSON parts.
Optional RFC6901 JSON pointer into JSON parts.

function.description: Search retained text; grouped hits list all offsets. Omitted row artifactRef inherits its page's reference.
function.name: search_tool_artifact

targetKind.description: Owner of the criterion identified by id. Omitted means artifact; turn selects an ordinary assistant Turn in this conversation.

function.description: Read this conversation’s versioned working facts and source freshness. Set include_tool_sources=true to list recent canonical tool observations available for quoted facts. Reuse exact observed or owner-assessed records instead of repeatedly reading unchanged source bodies. Derived claims need review; stale/unavailable records require new evidence. These records never grant tool authorization.
function.name: read_working_facts

targetKind.description: Owner of the criterion identified by id. Omitted means artifact; turn selects an ordinary assistant Turn in this conversation.

function.description: Save or revise a conversation working fact using the revision from read_working_facts. An observation must exactly quote one current artifact, acceptance criterion, file source, historical tool result, or observed fact. Criterion sources use targetKind=turn for ordinary task requirements; omitted targetKind means artifact. File sources require the id/version/path returned by read_files with bind_sources=true plus an exact quote. Use a tool source descriptor from read_working_facts(include_tool_sources=true) plus an exact quote. Tool observations are historical, not a check of current external state. Use derived for an inference: saving does not verify it. Sources bind exact digests/revisions. Owner-confirmed or corrected records cannot be overwritten; submit a new sourced proposal instead.
function.name: record_working_fact

id.description: Update only: an existing fact ID returned by read_working_facts. Omit id to create a new fact; the server assigns its ID. Never invent an ID.

revision.description: Current conversation aggregate revision from read_working_facts or the preceding successful record response; not an individual fact revision.

targetKind.description: Owner of the criterion identified by id. Omitted means artifact; turn selects an ordinary assistant Turn in this conversation.

text.description: For observation, copy the exact source quote as text, without a filename prefix, attribution or paraphrase. Use kind=derived for a summary or inference.

function.description:
Launch independent subtasks concurrently; use manage_agents for reusable workers. Returns an async handle immediately; results arrive as `<swarm-update>` messages. send_agent_message adds context using exact agent_id + swarm_run_id; get_agent_messages reads input receipts on demand. Messages grant no permissions. manage_agents assign starts an idle identity, never steers a live run.

Roles and exact tool scopes:
  - researcher: Open-ended research questions and information gathering — web searches, doc lookups, comparing libraries, surveying APIs. Choose this role when the answer requires reading multiple web pages or external sources. [tools: web_search, fetch_url, browser_research_page, browser_read_page, browser_list_tabs]
  - coder: Multi-file code investigations or modifications — find usages of X, audit a refactor, write a unit test, run a command and report. Use coder when the task touches code in the project. [tools: read_files, write_file, edit_file, search_files, find_files, run_command, poll, kill]
  - analyst: Quantitative analysis of data already on disk — log parsing, metric extraction, finding patterns in CSV / JSON / structured output. Choose this when the answer is numbers / tables. [tools: read_files, search_files, run_command, poll, kill]
  - browser: Tasks that require interacting with already-open browser tabs — click buttons, fill forms, scrape JS-rendered pages, take screenshots, or download a visible page asset into server staging. Use this when web_search / fetch_url cannot reach the content because it needs interaction. [tools: browser_list_tabs, browser_read_page, browser_research_page, browser_devtools, browser_execute_js, browser_screenshot, browser_click, browser_type, browser_press_key, browser_check, browser_select_option, browser_menu_click, browser_fill_form, browser_navigate, browser_close_tab, browser_preview_page, browser_download_url_to_server, fetch_url]
  - reviewer: Get a fresh, independent read on code or design — security review, bug hunting, code-style audit. Choose this for "second opinion" tasks where you want eyes that have not seen your analysis. Outputs a concrete punch list. [tools: read_files, search_files, find_files, run_command, poll, kill]
  - writer: Compose a long-form document — release notes, README sections, design docs, migration guides — from raw inputs you already have. Choose this when the task is mostly prose generation. [tools: read_files, write_file, search_files]
  - general: Mixed / unclear tasks where no single specialist role fits — a sub-task that needs a couple of different tool families together. Default fallback when in doubt. [tools: ALL tools minus ask_human/consider_project_message/get_agent_result/get_project_messages/list_agents/manage_agents/send_project_message/set_approval_delegate/spawn_agents]
  Every role additionally receives the shared artifact tools: store_artifact, read_artifact, list_artifacts.
  Team messages when granted: get_agent_messages, send_agent_message.

Choose this for 2+ independent branches or context isolation; keep trivial or sequential work local. Delegate MCP tools via the `tools` allowlist instead of loading them yourself. If the task needs a tool not listed by any specialist, use 'general'. Sub-agents cannot spawn or ask the user; provide self-contained objectives. When a worker reports a missing tool, Re-spawn the same task with general or a covering role; preserve scope.

Put all parallel agents in one `agents[]` call. Use `depends_on` only for a true prerequisite; otherwise maximize parallelism. This is fire-and-forget: continue useful local work or end the turn for automatic delivery. Do not sleep, predict results, or read `output_file` for progress. If only waiting remains, use `poll(ids=[<returned agent ids>], wait_s=1500, mode='any')`, which returns as soon as an agent finishes; no-id `poll` is a dashboard, not a wait. Each completion arrives with the agent's full result; `get_agent_result` re-reads it later by agent id and swarm_run_id, also after the run ends. A running main agent receives individual results at round boundaries; an idle conversation is auto-resumed only after the whole swarm settles, subject to Stop. Agents launched during such an automatic continuation never wake another one; their results arrive with the next turn. Failures may trigger one bounded diagnosis/closure pass, not an unlimited retry loop. Do not promise a wakeup on each agent completion or treat failed work as side-effect-free.

Each objective states the goal and why, needed context, paths, constraints, and expected bounded output. The root synthesizes results.
function.name: spawn_agents

agents.description: All parallel subtasks in one call; do not issue serial spawn calls.

context.description: Optional paths, data, constraints, or links.

depends_on.description: Sibling ids that must finish first. Use only for true prerequisites.

id.description: Optional sibling-reference id. Set it when another item names it in `depends_on`; omission mints an id unavailable to same-call dependencies.

objective.description: Self-contained goal, rationale, necessary context, and expected output. Required unless the agent's template has one, which precedes it.

output_schema.description: JSON Schema (type object) for the final answer; the result is compact JSON.

params.description: Template values, appended as a sorted list.

required_for_completion.description: Required delivery dependency; false only for optional exploration. Unresolved required work remains waiting after this turn ends.

role.description: Specialist role; defaults to `general`. Exact scopes are listed above.

template.description: A `templates` name: its objective and context precede this agent's; its role, tools and output_schema apply unless set here.

tools.description: Tool-name allowlist (e.g. ['mcp__github__get_issue']); narrow-only, intersected with role scope.

templates.description: Shared presets by name: {objective?, context?, role?, tools?, output_schema?}.

function.description:
Fetch the FULL final answer of one or more completed sub-agents again. Completion updates already carry the full result — use this to re-read an earlier result after it aged out of your context.

Results are durable per run: pass `swarm_run_id` (from the spawn_agents handle or a `<swarm-update>`) to read a run of this conversation that has ended, was evicted after inactivity, or was replaced by a later wave. Without it, ids resolve in the current swarm.

For MULTIPLE agents in one call, provide an `agent_ids` array — all results come back together in a single `results` list. This is much better than issuing several separate get_agent_result calls: prefer ONE batched call when you want the full bodies of the agents a `spawn_agents` wave produced.

For agents that are still running, the entry reports a running-status notice; for unknown ids it reports an error — neither aborts the rest of the batch.
function.name: get_agent_result

agent_id.description: A single agent id from a `<swarm-update>` payload or the spawn_agents handle. Single-fetch mode; omit when using `agent_ids`.

agent_ids.description: Array of agent ids to fetch in ONE call (batch mode). All results are returned together in the `results` field. Use INSTEAD of `agent_id` when you need several agents' full bodies — do NOT issue N separate get_agent_result calls.

swarm_run_id.description: Exact run handle: `swarm_run_id` of the spawn_agents handle or `<swarm-run-id>` of a `<swarm-update>`. Needed for an ended, evicted or earlier wave; omit for the current swarm.

function.description: Delegate tool-call approval decisions to a bounded adjudicator sub-agent governed by a natural-language policy you write. While a policy is active, a gated tool call (e.g. a destructive run_command) is judged against the policy FIRST: a clear approve executes without prompting the human, a clear deny rejects the call with the reason returned to you, and anything uncertain falls back to the human approval gate. Use this to keep working autonomously through batches of predictable approvals. The policy is task-scoped, never widens what the gate allows, and never applies to sub-agents. Requires an attended session.
function.name: set_approval_delegate

enabled.description: false clears the active policy; default true.

model_tier.description: Adjudicator model tier (default 'light'). Choose 'standard' for subtle policies.

policy.description: Natural-language approval rules the adjudicator applies verbatim, e.g. 'Allow read-only build and test commands; deny anything touching git remotes, package managers, or files outside the project.' Required when enabling.

timeout_seconds.description: Adjudicator wall-clock budget per decision (default 30, range 5..120). On timeout the call falls back to the human gate.

tools.description: Tool names this policy covers (default ['run_command']). Explicit names only — no wildcards.

function.description: Send one durable message to exactly one target. Two target forms exist; choose one and do not mix their fields. Form A, exact run: pass agent_id AND swarm_run_id from a launch handle. This steers or informs a running temporary spawn_agents child or the coordinator (set agent_id equal to swarm_run_id); it never starts or redirects work after that run ends. Example: {"agent_id":"child","swarm_run_id":"launch","content":"Evidence","idempotency_key":"evidence-1"}. Form B, stable colleague: pass retained_agent_id (from manage_agents/list_agents); optional scope selects the project or conversation binding, and intent=resume explicitly authorizes a fresh turn after cancellation. A busy colleague receives the message in its current owned assignment; an idle one starts a fresh turn with remembered dialogue and current tools, policy and budget. Supply a unique idempotency_key and reuse unchanged content, kind and intent after uncertainty; use get_agent_messages to reconcile the same stable key or exact run. Submission or turn start is not input confirmation, acceptance or completion. Stop work via kill, not natural language.
function.name: send_agent_message

agent_id.description: Exact team assignment ID; workers may target their coordinator with agent_id equal to swarm_run_id. Requires swarm_run_id; omit retained_agent_id.

content.description: Use readable prose and preserve exact identifiers and meaningful whitespace. The authored text is saved verbatim.

intent.description: Stable target only; omit for exact-run targets. Stable messaging defaults to message. resume explicitly authorizes a fresh turn after cancellation; it does not replay interrupted work.

retained_agent_id.description: Stable colleague identity; omit both run-target fields.

scope.description: Stable target only. Defaults to current project, otherwise conversation.

function.description: Read durable message evidence for exactly one target without starting work. Two target forms exist; choose one and do not mix their fields. Form A, exact run: pass agent_id AND swarm_run_id, plus optional message_id, to inspect input receipts in a temporary spawn_agents run, including a worker's own inbox. Example: {"agent_id":"child","swarm_run_id":"launch"}. Form B, stable colleague: pass retained_agent_id AND the original idempotency_key, plus optional scope, to inspect that message's pinned assignment and outcome; stable-agent reads remain root-only. Read on demand after uncertainty; input_confirmed does not prove acceptance or completion. Old messages never steer or activate replacement runs.
function.name: get_agent_messages

idempotency_key.description: Required for a stable-agent receipt lookup.

function.description: Read an owned long-horizon research/exploration plan, or a page of its experiment receipts. Use view=catalog without program_id to find existing plans; follow next_cursor with cursor. Reading never starts or resumes work. Use the same program_id across Chat turns; detail_path opens the full existing notebook with plans, evidence, independent reviews and costs. Report confirmed state and unknowns, not invented progress percentages.
function.name: get_exploration

function.description: Operate the same durable exploration plan shown in the long-horizon notebook from Chat. Use when the human requests sustained research, experiments or an independently reviewed deliverable. For create, supply the agreed objective, acceptance checks and applicable installed skill IDs in request; use start=true when execution is already requested, otherwise save the plan. Do not send the user to fill another form. Current Chat project, model and explicitly selected skills are inherited when omitted. For create/append/guide, reuse idempotency_key and identical arguments after an uncertain response; never create replacement work to retry. Use command with program_id and expected_version from the latest state_version to start, pause, resume, retry or cancel. If command acknowledgement is uncertain or the version changed, read current state before deciding again; do not replay an old control. guide requires expected_run_id from current_experiment and delivers a supplementary instruction to that experiment only; it does not rewrite the frozen original goal. append adds owner-requested experiments before the original final audit. Summarize the result in Chat and link detail_path for the full record. Creation/loading is not acceptance, publication permission or scientific evidence. The durable plan continues after this Chat turn ends; stopping Chat alone does not cancel it.
function.name: manage_exploration

function.description: Check or wait on background work: background shell commands (bg_* handles from run_command background=true), swarm sub-agents from spawn_agents, or tasks running in other conversations. With no id, returns a snapshot of everything currently running. With an id, returns that handle's status — and its full result once finished. Set wait_s to block until completion: the wait returns as soon as the handle finishes, new input arrives for this turn, or the task is stopped, so a long wait costs no extra model requests (capped at 1500 s = 25 minutes; on cap returns the running snapshot — call again to keep waiting). Background command completions are also delivered automatically, so only wait when there is nothing else to do.
function.name: poll

id.description: One handle: a bg_* command id, a swarm agent id, or a task id. Legacy aliases command_id / agent_id / task_id are accepted.

mode.description: With multiple swarm-agent ids: 'any' (default) returns as soon as one finishes; 'all' waits for every match.

wait_s.description: Seconds to block waiting for completion (at most 1500; returns as soon as the handle finishes). Omit for an instant snapshot.

function.description: Stop background work by handle: a bg_* background command (its process tree receives SIGTERM then SIGKILL) or a RUNNING swarm sub-agent. There is no timeout auto-kill — this is how background work is stopped. Tasks in other conversations cannot be killed from here; use that conversation's Stop control. Call poll with no arguments first if unsure what is running.
function.name: kill

id.description: Handle to stop: a bg_* command id or a swarm agent id. Legacy alias command_id is accepted.

function.description: List reusable team agents in the current project or conversation. Pass agent_id to inspect one agent and a bounded view of its remembered recent dialogue. This is read-only; use manage_agents to create, assign, reset, archive, restore, or delete.
function.name: list_agents

scope.description: Omit to use the current default scope.

function.description: Manage reusable team agents. A retained agent remembers prior assignments across turns and restarts while using no worker when idle. Use spawn_agents for one-off independent work. Create once, then assign later objectives by agent_id; the assignment runs as an ordinary async Swarm child and returns via <swarm-update>. Assign requires an idle identity; a busy agent rejects another assignment. Use send_agent_message with retained_agent_id to message this colleague: busy adds input to the owned current assignment; idle starts the next turn with saved dialogue. Cancelled colleagues require intent=resume. For steering only, send the exact agent_id plus swarm_run_id; it never starts replacement work. Use get_agent_messages with the original target and idempotency_key to reconcile uncertainty. Do not treat assign as live steering. Scope defaults to the current project, or conversation when no project is attached. Current tool permissions apply on every run. Use list_agents to inspect a bounded memory view. Reset clears working memory; archive pauses assignments; delete removes the retained record. Promote copies a completed temporary Swarm child in this conversation into a new retained identity.
function.name: manage_agents

abandon.description: For reset of a busy agent: fence its late memory result.

agent_id.description: Required except for create and list.

scope.description: Omit to use the current default scope.

source_agent_id.description: Completed Swarm child ID for promote.

tools.description: Optional narrow-only tool allowlist for this run.

function.description: Publish an existing document or attachment from verified task project roots into an owned durable artifact. Use after generating HTML/Markdown/SVG/text/PDF/ZIP/office files, including self-contained interactive prototypes. A workspace path is not a web URL. Returns verified byte/hash metadata and browser delivery URLs; reference the artifact ID with native open/download actions. Safe preview blocks document scripts by default; script execution is a separate human choice. Multi-file directories are not mounted or dependency-resolved. Never publish private files without user authorization.
function.name: publish_response_file

function.description: Publish a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF from verified task project roots as an owned durable response image. Use explicitly after run_command image generation. Never publish shell-output paths automatically.
function.name: publish_response_asset

function.description: Publish a native interactive workspace: optional stack/grid/tabs layout groups, metric_grid indicators with unknown values and trends, workflow progress and next steps, notice explanations, resource_panel live compute capacity (provider ID from environment_providers/compute_catalog; use connection for an owned MCP server exposing read-only compute_catalog; for get_queue_resource use provider=queue, connection and exact queue), measured comparison/chart, general data_chart (line/scatter/bar/pie), timing diagram (timeline), table, image gallery, supplied-source citations, server-issued choice_prompt or form_prompt (ask_human free_text/batch), evidence, artifact reference or read-only actions. Prefer native blocks over ASCII diagrams or code-only answers when these components fit the explanation. Data is schema-validated and rendered automatically in this tool card and the artifact panel; retain a concise textual answer as fallback. For inline answers you may also emit the same valid JSON in a tofu-ui fenced block. Only owned same-conversation asset/artifact IDs are permitted. Publish local PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF through publish_response_asset first; never use workspace paths as image URLs. Relative improvement cannot override failed or unknown acceptance. Citation blocks contain supplied HTTP(S) sources; reference them in prose as [[cite:blockId/sourceId]]. Previews never fetch or claim source verification. choice_prompt/form_prompt only references an existing ask_human interactionId; question/options/answer state come from the owned server turn, never this payload. Use ask_human to create a real question, not invented IDs. Resource panels refresh through the owned task/run provider connection without model polling; snapshots are historical evidence. Headless Evolution publication is saved in the existing tool result, with no invented conversation. No model HTML or JavaScript executes.
function.name: publish_rich_response
